clue.text: Ain't twisting, yet five couples must have a knees-up here

indicators.note: twisting the short word around rearranges its four letters

parts.note: five couples are ten people
a knees-up is British slang for a lively party with dancing

explanation.surface: A tipsy dance caller insists that, slang notwithstanding, ten dancers must turn out for the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' rearranges AINT into INAT. A knees-up is a British party, here a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in attendance is present, which is what being here means.

clue.text: Actress inexperienced in general use, losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word use drops out

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a green actress is in widespread use but has lost her spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' takes the central S out of USE to leave UE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is a naive young woman, especially the stock role of an inexperienced girl played by an actress.

clue.text: Forgive sailor catching fish — about five

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: about means the fish surrounds the next piece

parts.note: sole is a flatfish
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A fisherman pardons the sailor who has caught about five fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' only links sailor to the rest; 'about' wraps the fish round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to release them from guilt, which is to forgive them.

clue.text: Inaction's outrageous for a conductor

indicators.note: outrageous suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word with its S included supplies the nine letters

explanation.surface: Someone complains that doing nothing is shocking behaviour for an orchestra's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian orchestral conductor, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: They are hard and make trouble in two directions

indicators.note: in places the trouble between the two compass letters

parts.note: N and S are the compass points north and south
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Some tough people cause problems wherever they go, this way and that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AIL between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nails are hard metal spikes, and 'hard as nails' is proverbial toughness.

clue.text: One revolutionary paper gets left in this dress

parts.note: one can be written as the article a

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the five letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A radical newspaper is turned out in this garb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the article A here, not the numeral I; 'in this dress' points to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, which is what dress means as a general noun.

clue.text: Half China's opposed to Italian wine

indicators.note: half asks for the first part of the country's name

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

explanation.surface: Part of China is said to object to a wine from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes CHI, the front of CHINA; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Long sleeper had to rent carrier with shellfish

parts.note: to rent is to tear, to rip
a van carries goods
a winkle is a small edible sea snail

explanation.surface: Someone had to hire a lorry to carry seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' here is the verb to tear, not the money paid for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: Rip Van Winkle is the Washington Irving character who slept for twenty years.

clue.text: Takes in food but is keeping gents shivering

indicators.note: keeping means the two letters hold the rest inside them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shivering suggests shaking, so the letters of gents are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man eats while his shivering male companions are kept indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes in food' reads as a phrase in the surface, but it is the whole definition; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to swallow and absorb food into the body.

clue.text: One MP is attracted by German song, as suggested

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP, Member of Parliament, taken as written
a Lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: A British politician is drawn to German songs, as hinted.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lied (plural Lieder) is a German art song of the Schubert kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied was hinted at rather than stated, which is to say suggested.

clue.text: Conflict? What makes it seem danger?

indicators.note: the solution, read as a word for disarrangement, is itself what jumbles these words into it

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks what makes a quarrel look so threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that DIS-AGREEMENT, read as 'disarrangement', describes the anagram itself: jumble IT SEEM DANGER and you get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A disagreement is a dispute, a clash of views, so it is a form of conflict.

clue.text: Plain vehicle: one taking everything back

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: back means the word for everything is read in reverse

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: An ordinary vehicle with one item taking everything back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is used informally for plain or ordinary, without extras.

clue.text: They play together but stone mobs

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
rings are gangs or cartels

explanation.surface: Players unite, yet hurl stones at crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: The strings of an orchestra are the section of stringed instruments that play together.

clue.text: Sister's child needs some condemnation, ie censure

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A girl's niece deserves a bit of harsh criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'needs' into the definition; it is the link between definition and wordplay, and 'Sister's child' alone is the niece.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's sibling, so a sister's child is one.

clue.text: As a result of prosecuting, the lieutenant is held to be offensive

indicators.note: is held means the officer is enclosed by the other phrase

parts.note: in suing means in the course of or through taking legal action
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A court case decides that an officer's remarks were abusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is held' puts LT inside IN SUING.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulting remarks are rude and hurtful, which is what offensive means.

clue.text: Another patient man is moonlighting

parts.note: a second is another one
Job of the Bible is the byword for patience

explanation.surface: A second long-suffering man is working nights.
explanation.walkthrough: The patience of Job is proverbial.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonlighting is holding an extra job on the side, usually in secret.

clue.text: I cannot sleep much in masonic clothes

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: clothes is read as a verb, dressing the letters in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Freemason complains that his regalia keeps him awake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' rearranges MASONIC into SOMNIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: An insomniac is a person who has difficulty sleeping, so could say this of themselves.

clue.text: Sunday in church has religious education, which is not affected

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: On Sundays the church offers religious teaching that is unpretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) and RE (Religious Education, a British school subject) are common abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sincere is genuine, free of pretence, so not affected.

clue.text: Doctor goes this way and that with Anthea not half sarcastic

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: the doctor appears both as written and turned backwards

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: not half keeps only the first part of the girl's name

explanation.surface: A doctor wavers, joined by a half-hearted Anthea in a cutting mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' gives both MO and DR, the latter reversed to RD by 'goes this way and that'. 'not half' leaves ANT of ANTHEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant humour is biting and caustic, close in sense to sarcastic.

clue.text: Large gun found in search

definitions.meaning: a firearm with a long ... barrel, bigger than a pistol
to ransack or go through something hunting for valuables

explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long gun, and to rifle through something is to search it.

clue.text: Australian bird got up and everyone turned over

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up

indicators.note: turned over means the word for everyone is reversed

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A bird from Australia got up and everyone rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses ALL to LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The rosella is a brightly coloured Australian parrot.

clue.text: Exotic ring held in place by crooked finger

indicators.note: held in place by means the ring is enclosed by the jumbled letters
crooked suggests bent out of shape, so the letters of finger are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: An unusual ring is kept on by a bent finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' turns FINGER into FREIGN, and 'held in place by' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic means coming from a foreign country, strange and unfamiliar.

clue.text: The family will want warm claret, perhaps

parts.note: warm-hearted, kind
claret is an example of red wine

explanation.surface: The relatives will be asking for mulled claret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warm' is warm-hearted, not heated; 'perhaps' marks claret as one example of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred are one's relatives, a family taken together.

clue.text: Duck makes eg odd stew

indicators.note: stew suggests mixing ingredients together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe says the duck makes an unusual casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird in a stew; it is the verb, to evade.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to dodge it, avoiding it by a quick move.

clue.text: No very good person needs spirit as a cure-all

parts.note: taken as written
ST, saint, is a very good person
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: No saint needs liquor as a universal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: ST for saint is a crossword convention for a good person.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy, often one claimed to cure everything.

clue.text: Boy always takes a short road

parts.note: ever means always
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A lad always takes the shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short road' gives the abbreviation RD.
explanation.definitionFit: Everard is a boy's given name.

clue.text: Girl, sick one in a winter month

indicators.note: in places the sick one inside the month

parts.note: Jan is short for January
ill means sick
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A girl falls ill one January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a winter month' is January in the northern hemisphere, abbreviated in the usual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Jillian is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Frivolous person's performance touches her understanding

parts.note: a feat is an accomplishment, a performance
taken as written
brain means intelligence or understanding

explanation.surface: A scatterbrain's act shows how much she understands.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is just 'is', linking definition to wordplay; 'touches' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A featherbrain is a silly, flighty person, so frivolous.
